source_text.ISS-0937:
id: ISS-0937
title: "Backend CI red at UTC month boundary: TenantTemplateTest parity (extra events_y2026m09) and PartitionMaintenance/RetentionOperations/EventRetention tests ({:error,:partition_not_eligible}) fail on 2026-10-01"
discovered_by: ELIXIR-DEV
discovered_in_run: WF03-ISS0930-20261001 (Step Final, PR #2076; filed by ORCH)
discovered_at: "2026-10-01T00:21:56Z"
severity: MAJOR
description: >
  PR #2076 (scripts/fixtures-only, no lib/ or migration change) had its backend job fail twice. Run 1: one TenantTemplateTest
  parity failure extra=["events_y2026m09"]. Re-run after the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01 UTC rollover: 12 failures in
  PartitionMaintenanceTest, RetentionOperationsTest, EventRetentionTest ({:error, :partition_not_eligible}). Hypothesis, not
  reproduced on main: the tests depend on the real current UTC month / partition eligibility and break at the month boundary.
  PR #2076 was merged with --admin per decision 0018. Confirm via main's CI on ed40c2fa, then make the tests clock-independent.
affected_files:
  - test/letflow/events/ (partition maintenance / retention tests)
  - test/letflow/tenants/ (tenant template parity test)
queue_ref: Q-920  # queue issue_ref ISS-0920 collides with an existing local file; local filename ISS-0937
github_ref: GH-2077
status: open

task.description: WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup in docs/issues/*.yaml for resolved entries about partitions, events_y*, retention, month-boundary/clock-dependent tests, TenantTemplateTest parity) + Step 1 (diagnose), combined. DEFECT: backend CI went red at the UTC month boundary 2026-09-30 -> 2026-10-01. PR #2076 runs: GitHub Actions run 36793410900 (backend job started 2026-10-01T00:06Z) failed with ~12 failures in PartitionMaintenanceTest / RetentionOperationsTest / EventRetentionTest ({:error, :partition_not_eligible}); an earlier run failed TenantTemplateTest parity with extra=[events_y2026m09] (that earlier run's logs: use `gh run list --branch feature/WF03-ISS0930-20261001` + `gh run view <id> --log-failed`; strip noise with grep -E 'test/.*exs:[0-9]+|tests, |failures|extra|partition_not_eligible' - the logs are huge, never dump them whole). Main's own CI runs: 36795709173 (commit ed40c2fa) and 36795979277 (commit 590c923f) were still running at dispatch; poll them (`gh run view <id> --json status,conclusion,jobs`) and report whether main is currently RED or GREEN with the failing test names if red. NOTE a pull_request run on a docs-only chore branch at 2026-10-01T00:22Z had its backend job succeed in 52s - check whether backend gate is path-filtered/skipped for docs-only changes (so its success proves nothing) before using it as evidence. TASK: determine the TRUE root cause with evidence, not hypothesis. Read the failing tests and the code they exercise (partition maintenance/retention/events partition creation, tenant template build, Letflow.Tenants / TenantProvisioning partition creation; find the modules by grep for 'events_y', 'partition_not_eligible', 'PartitionMaintenance', 'EventRetention', 'RetentionOperations', 'TenantTemplate'). Determine for each failing test: how does it derive 'now' / current month (DateTime.utc_now, Date.utc_today, a clock option/injection, a migration that creates events_yYYYmMM partitions for a fixed window, a template fixture?), and why does a month rollover break it. Decide whether the fix belongs in (a) tests (make them clock-independent / derive from the same clock source), (b) the production partition-creation code (e.g. the template/migration pre-creates partitions relative to build time so the parity comparison differs; or partitions for the new current month are not being created/eligible), or (c) both; state which, and why. Distinguish a real production defect (e.g. next-month partition not created in time at a real month boundary -> inserts failing in prod) from a test-only brittleness. REPRODUCE: locally with a controllable clock if feasible. The worktree has no deps/_build: you may run `mix deps.get`/compile there, or reuse the main checkout's compiled artifacts by setting MIX_BUILD_PATH / copying deps (do NOT modify the main checkout's tree, never switch branches there). A local Postgres for this workspace is configured via .env (LETFLOW_DB_PORT, 5482; already copied to the worktree; do not print secrets); start it with `docker compose up -d` in the WORKTREE only if not already reachable (check with a quick connect first). Today's real UTC date is already 2026-10-01 so the failing tests should reproduce for real right now: run the failing test files (mix test test/letflow/... --seed 0 etc.) and quote real failure output. Then, if feasible, reproduce the PASSING case by faking the clock back to September (e.g. `faketime`/libfaketime isn't available on Windows - instead look for an injectable clock/`:now` option or Application env the code already supports; if none exists, say so and prove the dependency by reading the code and by a small mix run that calls the partition-eligibility function with a September timestamp vs an October one). Do NOT implement the fix. Work ONLY in the worktree in context.worktree (never the main checkout C:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-4; do not switch branches anywhere). Do not commit; ORCH commits. Do not edit any file except this handoff. Fill result in this handoff file; set status IN_PROGRESS at claim, then COMPLETED/FAILED with result.status PASS/FAIL. result.summary MUST contain: registry lookup result; root cause with file:line citations; for each of the 4 test groups the clock source and why it breaks; main's CI state (run ids, conclusions, failing tests); whether it is test-only or production-affecting and why; recommended fix location and concrete change list (files, approach: e.g. an injectable clock / derive expectations from the same function the code uses / freeze via Application env); whether a fail-first regression test is feasible (it must be able to FAIL on pre-fix code under a simulated month-boundary clock regardless of the real date - say how), and the owned_modules the fix will write (put them in result.owned_modules too). next_action: 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design'.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause named with file:line citations and real failure output quoted
Main CI state (red/green) stated with run ids
Test-only vs production defect decided with reasoning
Fix location and concrete change list decided
Fail-first regression approach under a simulated clock stated
No files modified other than this handoff

result.summary:
REGISTRY LOOKUP (Step 0.5): grep of docs/issues/ for events_y|partition_not_eligible|month.boundary|TenantTemplate hit ISS-0423, ISS-0481, ISS-0515, ISS-0853 (all resolved) plus ISS-0937 itself. None concerns a clock/month-dependent test or partition-window drift (0423 = suite serial runtime, 0481 = INV-1 async enforcement, 0515 = template build race, 0853 = unrelated). No prior resolved entry matches; NOT a recurrence. First occurrence of this class.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by real reproduction on 2026-10-01 UTC): TEST-ONLY wall-clock brittleness at the UTC month boundary, two independent mechanisms. lib/ production code is correct.

(A) eligible_past_month off-by-one on the 1st of every month (PartitionMaintenanceTest / RetentionOperationsTest / EventRetentionTest, {:error,:partition_not_eligible}). Production rule lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex:360-363: eligible?(y,m) = Date.utc_today() >= first_day_of_next_month(y,m) + min_partition_age_days. Tests override min_partition_age_days to 1 and use 'last calendar month' as the always-eligible fixture: partition_maintenance_test.exs:237 (`eligible_past_month = shift_months(current_month(), -1)`; current_month at :195-198 uses Date.utc_today()), retention_operations_test.exs:143 (current_month :122-125), routers/event_retention_test.exs:71-73. For M = last month, next_month_start = 1st of the CURRENT month, cutoff = 2nd; today >= cutoff is false exactly when today is the 1st (true on days 2..31) -> {:error, :partition_not_eligible}. The comment at partition_maintenance_test.exs:234-237 ('always eligible ... regardless of which day') is wrong. Breaks on the 1st of EVERY month, not only October; was green on the 30th. Real local output (MIX_ENV=test, seed 0, partition_maintenance_test.exs): 8+ failures, e.g. '1) test AC2/EO-001 -- whole-partition DDL only issues zero per-row DELETE/row-scoped INSERT ... right: {:error, :partition_not_eligible}', '6) test EO-003 ... partition_maintenance_test.exs:798', plus 'correction (a)', 'correction (b)', '§4.4b ...', 'EO-002 ...', 'crash-recovery ... :already_retired' (all `right: {:error, :partition_not_eligible}`). The test at :893 (current month ineligible under the 400-day default) passes. I did not separately run retention_operations_test.exs and event_retention_test.exs locally; their failure is established by identical code (same eligible_past_month, same eligible?/2 path via RetentionOperations.retire/skip handling at retention_operations.ex:267) and by CI run 36793410900 output reported in the issue. Clock sources: PartitionMaintenanceTest = Date.utc_today() in current_month/0 (:195) + production Date.utc_today() in eligible?/2 (:363); RetentionOperationsTest = Date.utc_today() in current_month/0 (:122) -> eligible_past_month (:143), used at :213-218, :306, :346, :407, and PartitionMaintenance.eligible_months/1 (:224-236); EventRetentionTest = Date.utc_today() at event_retention_test.exs:72, used at :208 (route -> RetentionOperations -> retire_month -> eligible?/2).

(B) TenantTemplateTest parity: extra=["events_y2026m09"]. test/support/tenant_template_test.exs:93 ('template matches an independently migration-built reference schema') and :108 ('two concurrent reference-schema builds do not collide') call Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.assert_template_parity_against_independent_reference!/0 (test/support/tenant_template.ex:646-680), which replays all migrations into a fresh reference schema NOW and diffs it against the persistent 'tenant_template' schema built earlier. Migration priv/repo/migrations/20260922000002_create_events_p_initial_partitions.exs:39-59 creates events_yYYYYmMM for [data-min-month or current month .. current month+2] using Date.utc_today() at migration RUN time: a template built in September holds events_y2026m09..m11, a reference replayed in October holds m10..m12. check_table_set/2 (tenant_template.ex:1207-1222) filters req376 partition tables only from the `missing` side; `extra = MapSet.difference(cand_tables, ref_tables)` is unfiltered, so the template's stale m09 table is reported (dim #1). In CI the rollover occurred INSIDE one run: run 36793410900 created 2026-09-30T23:53:38Z, backend job started 00:06:31Z (failed step 'Run backend gate', ended 00:19:12Z); the earlier run's template was built before midnight, parity ran after. Local reproduction (real): the stale September 'tenant_template' persisted in the test DB still passes template_db_state/0 (tenant_template.ex:325-334; fingerprint = md5 of migration version list only, :341-350, no date), so `mix test test/support/tenant_template_test.exs --seed 0` printed '1) test the template itself is faithful to a genuine migration build template matches an independently migration-built reference schema ... [dim #1] table set: extra=["events_y2026m09"]' (test :93) and '2) ... two concurrent reference-schema builds do not collide ... [dim #1] table set: extra=["events_y2026m09"]' (test :108). Tenant fixtures cloned from the template are unaffected (clones are unpartitioned; req376_partition_management_table? filters them).

Not diagnosed: why runs 36793256609 / 36793096870 (23:49-23:52Z, before rollover) failed within 1-2 min; not examined, believed unrelated (ISS-0930 branch work in flight).

MAIN CI STATE: NOT yet decided at time of writing. Run 36795709173 (commit ed40c2fa, push to main): status in_progress; Detect changed paths success, Mobile gate success, Frontend gate success, Backend gate (mix letflow.check) in_progress. Run 36795979277 (commit 590c923f): status pending, no jobs yet. Both are dated 2026-10-01 so I EXPECT RED with the same failures (expectation, not observation); ORCH must re-poll `gh run view 36795709173 --json status,conclusion,jobs`. Last known green main CI: 36785684070 (commit 4bb82d12, 2026-09-30T22:27Z). The docs-only branch backend success (52s) is NOT evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:144-200 sets backend=true only if changed files match ^(lib/|priv/repo/migrations/|test/|mix.exs|mix.lock|.tool-versions|config/|.github/workflows/ci.yml); docs-only PRs get backend=false and the expensive steps are skipped (steps `if: needs.changes.outputs.backend != 'false'`). Push-to-main always runs every gate (ISS-0840), so main's runs are real.

TEST-ONLY vs PRODUCTION: test-only. (1) eligible?/2 is a retire-eligibility rule for months at least min_partition_age_days (default 400) old; being false for a 1-day-old month is correct, nothing is wrongly blocked or lost. (2) Production partition pre-creation ensure_future_partitions/2 (partition_maintenance.ex:139-155; months_window uses Date.utc_today() at call time, lookahead @default_months_ahead 2) is driven by Letflow.Scheduler (scheduler.ex:101, :763-769; scheduler/poller.ex:401), keeping current+2 months ahead, so at a real month boundary the next month's partition already exists; events_default is an additional safety net. No evidence of a production insert failure. Minor doc/code inconsistency noted, out of scope: doc at partition_maintenance.ex:75-76 says 'today >= last_day(M) + N' while code uses first_day(M+1) + N (one day later); harmless.

RECOMMENDED FIX LOCATION: (a) tests / test support only; no lib/ or migration change. Both defects are in how tests/test template relate to wall-clock month; the production clock reads are correct, and an injectable clock in lib/ would widen scope for no production benefit.

CONCRETE CHANGE LIST (for CODE-DESIGNER):
1. Retention tests (3 files): replace eligible_past_month = current-1 with a month eligible on EVERY day of the current month under min_partition_age_days=1, i.e. current-2 (cutoff = 2nd of last month <= any day of current month). Preferably extract one shared pure helper (e.g. new test/support/partition_clock.ex, `Letflow.Test.PartitionClock.eligible_past_month(today :: Date.t())` returning shift_months({today.year,today.month}, -2)) replacing the three duplicated private current_month/shift_months/eligible_past_month copies; correct the misleading comment at partition_maintenance_test.exs:234-237. Per-test checks: retention_operations_test.exs:217 (older = eligible_past_month shifted -3), :218 ('newer'); partition_maintenance_test.exs:434 (ensure_future_partitions window starts at the current month so a current-2 fixture does not collide); the EO-003 'instance spanning two months' test (~:778-798) must not rely on the month directly before the current one; event_retention_test.exs:84/208; confirm create_events_month_partition!/3 for current-2 does not overlap events_default rows.
2. Template parity (test/support/tenant_template.ex check_table_set/2, ~:1207-1222): the dynamic events_yYYYYmMM / events_archive_yYYYYmMM set is time-dependent by design (Letflow.TenantFixture.req376_partition_management_table?/1 already documents this), so also reject req376_partition_management_table? tables from the `extra` side while still failing on any non-partition extra/missing table; structure of events/events_default stays covered by the other dimensions (constraints :1218, :1371 already filter via the same predicate). Update the comment at ~:1195-1205 accordingly. Tolerates the mid-run rollover. Optional hardening (not sufficient alone, because CI's rollover is mid-run after the template is built): include {year,month} in migration_fingerprint_comment (:341-350) so a persistent local DB rebuilds its template on a new month.
3. Do not change PartitionMaintenance.eligible?/2 or the migration.

FAIL-FIRST REGRESSION APPROACH (feasible, clock-independent, no real-date dependence): (i) Eligibility: the shared helper takes `today` as an argument, so a test iterates `today` over every day of >= 24 consecutive months (including every 1st, Dec->Jan, a leap day) and asserts Date.compare(today, Date.add(first_day_of_month_after(eligible_past_month(today)), 1)) != :lt. With the pre-fix formula (-1) this fails for every 1st-of-month date; passes with -2. No DB, no clock. (ii) Parity: a test hand-builds two small schemas (reference: ordinary tables + events_default + events_y2026m10; candidate: same + events_y2026m09) and calls Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.assert_clone_parity!(ref, cand, dimensions: [1]); pre-fix it raises 'table set: extra=["events_y2026m09"]', post-fix it returns :ok; additionally a genuinely extra non-partition table (e.g. 'bogus_tbl') must still raise (guards against over-filtering). Both deterministic on any real date. End-to-end: ORCH can run the three retention test files and tenant_template_test.exs on the real date 2026-10-01 (currently failing; must pass after fix), also with the 'tenant_template' schema freshly dropped.

OWNED MODULES the fix will write (all test-side): test/support/tenant_template.ex; test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs; test/letflow/event_store/retention_operations_test.exs; test/letflow/routers/event_retention_test.exs; new test/support/partition_clock.ex (+ its test); new parity regression test (e.g. in test/support/tenant_template_test.exs). No lib/ or priv/repo/migrations changes; SECURITY-REVIEWER gate likely not triggered (no tenant-data path change); REVIEWER still applies.

ENVIRONMENT NOTE: reproduction used the main checkout's deps via MIX_DEPS_PATH (read-only) and a copy of its _build/test into the worktree's gitignored _build/; the main checkout was not touched; Postgres 5482 (letflow-4-postgres-1) was already running. The local letflow_test DB still holds the stale September 'tenant_template' schema (shared by the main checkout's tests); whoever verifies locally should drop it or rely on the fix.

next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design.
